gloss: to let pass; to ignore what one hears; to half-listen

definitions.gloss: to let pass; to ignore what one hears
definitions.explanation: to hear something but deliberately not react or respond to it
to listen without paying full attention, often as background

examples.japanese: {嫌味|いやみ}は{聞|き}き{流|なが}すに{限|かぎ}る。
examples.english: The best thing to do with snide remarks is to let them pass.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{私|わたし}の{忠告|ちゅうこく}を{聞|き}き{流|なが}した。
ラジオを{聞|き}き{流|なが}しながら{料理|りょうり}する。
examples.english: I cook while half-listening to the radio.

examples.japanese: {悪口|わるくち}は{聞|き}き{流|なが}すようにしている。
examples.english: I try to let bad-mouthing go in one ear and out the other.

examples.japanese: {音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}き{流|なが}す。
examples.english: To have music playing in the background.

examples.japanese: {小言|こごと}は{右|みぎ}から{左|ひだり}に{聞|き}き{流|なが}した。
examples.english: The scolding went in one ear and out the other.

notes:
{聞|き}き{流|なが}す has two main uses: deliberately ignoring what you hear, or casual background listening.

VERB TYPE:
- Godan verb (す-verb)
- Transitive

COMPOUND STRUCTURE:
- {聞|き}く (to hear/listen) + {流|なが}す (to let flow)
- Literally: to let what you hear flow away

SENSE 1 (IGNORING):
- Deliberate choice not to react
- Often a coping strategy for criticism
- {聞|き}き{流|なが}すに{限|かぎ}る (best to ignore) is a common phrase

SENSE 2 (BACKGROUND LISTENING):
- Not paying full attention
- Common with music, radio, podcasts
- Neutral/positive connotation

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {嫌味|いやみ}を{聞|き}き{流|なが}す (let snide remarks pass)
- {悪口|わるくち}を{聞|き}き{流|なが}す (let gossip pass)
- {忠告|ちゅうこく}を{聞|き}き{流|なが}す (ignore advice)
- {音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}き{流|なが}す (have music on in background)
- BGMを{聞|き}き{流|なが}す (have background music playing)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- {右|みぎ}から{左|ひだり}に{聞|き}き{流|なが}す (let go in one ear and out the other)
- {聞|き}き{流|なが}す{英語|えいご} (English for passive listening - book/course title pattern)

REGISTER: Neutral. Common in everyday conversation.
